title: Electronic Screening as a Design Lever in La-Doped BaTiO$_3$: Coupled Polarization, Dielectric Response, and Optical Anisotropy
abstract: Donor substitution can tune the coupled ferroelectric, dielectric, electronic, and optical properties of perovskite oxides by modifying lattice distortions and electronic screening. We investigate these effects in La-doped BaTiO3 using density functional theory, density-functional perturbation theory, and the Berry-phase formalism for polarization. For a model with 12.5% La substitution at the Ba site, La incorporation induces anisotropic lattice contraction, reduces tetragonality and Ti off-centering, and weakens the energetic stabilization of the tetragonal ferroelectric phase. The accompanying reduction in polarization is associated with enhanced electronic screening and reduced anomalous Born effective charges. Phonon calculations indicate that the relaxed doped structure is dynamically stable, while hardening of a low-frequency polar mode is consistent with weakened ferroelectricity. The high-frequency dielectric response increases moderately, whereas the static dielectric response decreases as the lattice contribution is suppressed. Electronic-structure calculations show a Fermi-level shift toward the conduction band without mid-gap defect states. The optical spectra exhibit an absorption-edge shift consistent with a Burstein-Moss-type mechanism, enhanced near-edge transparency, and reduced birefringence. Together, these results suggest a microscopic connection between donor-induced screening, polar-mode hardening, reduced dynamical charges, polarization suppression, and decreased optical anisotropy. The conclusions apply to the investigated 12.5% composition; calculations at additional concentrations are needed to establish quantitative doping trends.

title: Kinetic-inductance Parametric Amplification in Superconducting Hybrid Magnonics
abstract: Parametric amplification enables sensitive microwave detection and signal processing by amplifying weak signals with minimal added noise. Here, we demonstrate kinetic inductance mediated parametric amplification in a hybrid magnonic system comprising a nonlinear NbN nanowire resonator strongly coupled to a yttrium iron garnet sphere. The resonator exhibits four wave mixing and nonlinear frequency pulling, enabling parametric amplification both away from and within the magnon-photon strong coupling regime. In the magnon detuned regime, we observe 7 dB gain, while coupling to the YIG magnon shifts the parametric amplification response by ~20 MHz and yields 3.4 dB gain in the hybrid mode. Thus, magnon photon coupling provides a route to magnetically tune the spectral position of kinetic inductance parametric amplification. At higher pump powers, the system transitions to a self oscillatory regime featuring comb-like sidebands and probe activated nonlinear mode mixing. These results establish hybrid magnonics as a platform for tunable nonlinear microwave amplification and dynamics.

title: Orientation-selective microwave heating of laser-graphitized diamond at 2.45 GHz
abstract: Pristine diamond couples negligibly to a 2.45 GHz field. We show that femtosecond-laser inscription of a buried graphitic (sp2) architecture makes a 4 x 4 x 2 mm^3 N-doped (100 ppm) high-pressure high- temperature (HPHT) crystal absorb strongly, and that the absorption is switched by the orientation of the inscribed structure relative to the cavity electric field. With the 1.8 mm depth of a concentric grating along E, stepped power gave a smooth staircase to an indicated ~500C at 80 W followed, at 90 W, by an abrupt excursion to an indicated ~900C with surface roughening and terraced oxidation. Rotating the same sample so that the grating diameter lay along E, and an unmodified crystal in either orientation, gave no signal above the ~40C floor. We account for this by the depolarisation factors L of the sub-wavelength tracks, collapsed into one screening parameter S = L{\sigma}/({\omega}{\epsilon}0{\epsilon}h), here, {\sigma} conductivity, {\omega} - cyclic frequency, {\epsilon}h,0 - permittivity of host and vacuum, respectively. The model turns element length, diameter and writing regime into design variables for microwave absorption in a transparent host.

title: Chiral Cavity Vacua as Local Generators and Probes of Non-Abelian Kitaev Topology
abstract: We show how a gyrotropic cavity vacuum generates, probes, and spatially programs non-Abelian topology in the Kitaev honeycomb model. Gauge-consistent virtual-photon elimination produces a universal helicity-odd interaction $\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]$ alongside same-order even dressing. For the leading bond polarization, this commutator is exactly the Kitaev three-spin mass. Mode normalization imposes a thermodynamic constraint: one extended normalized mode gives a local mass that vanishes with sample area, whereas a localized mode writes a finite topological island and a finite mode density enables a bulk mass. The exact Majorana solution yields helicity-reversed Chern gaps and edge propagation, while integrated circular dichroism exactly measures the mass generator, $\langle\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]\rangle=-\sqrt3p^2\langle O_3\rangle$. Real-space calculations reveal a non-Abelian island and a helicity wall with two co-propagating Majorana modes. Uniform helicity reversal is a Dirac-mass quench with $n_{\rm ex}\propto\tau_Q^{-1}$, whereas moving a wall localizes the gap closing. The equilibrium vacuum kernel contains sum-frequency rather than resonant denominators. These results establish distinct criteria for local and bulk cavity-induced topology.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

title: From phase analysis to phase tracking: a robust approach to atomic-scale strain mapping
abstract: Atomic-scale strain governs the electronic, ferroic and mechanical properties of materials, and atomic-resolution microscopy measures it most directly. Geometric phase analysis (GPA) is the standard tool, but it fails when a Bragg reflection moves outside its fixed Fourier aperture under large strain or rotation, or in misoriented grains. Here we introduce geometric phase tracking analysis (GPTA), whose Fourier aperture tracks the Bragg reflection at each pixel in real space. A narrow aperture can therefore reject noise without losing a displaced reflection. On 13,795 simulated and experimental atomic-resolution images under various imaging conditions, GPTA reduces GPA's failure rate from 27% to 11.5% with up to 335 times better accuracy. It also gives strain and dislocation maps across grains, resistance to dynamical-scattering extinction, and a confidence map, capabilities that GPA lacks. Tracking the aperture combines reciprocal-space dose efficiency with real-space spatial resolution and extends atomic-scale strain metrology to beam-sensitive materials and challenging imaging conditions.

summaries.en: Geometric phase tracking analysis (GPTA) improves atomic-scale strain mapping by moving a narrow Fourier aperture to follow each Bragg reflection at every pixel, reducing the failure rate of geometric phase analysis from 27% to 11.

title: Broadband emitter localization and prefabrication two-photon interference from InAs/InP quantum dots monolithically grown on an InGaAsP/InP distributed Bragg reflector
abstract: We demonstrate a monolithic telecom C-band single-photon platform based on low-density InAs/InP quantum dots grown on an InGaAsP/InP distributed Bragg reflector, with simulated upward light-extraction efficiency exceeding 10% within the 40 nm spectral band. Enhanced light extraction is crucial for wide-field photoluminescence imaging, enabling approximately 3 nm statistical centroid-localization precision of QD emitters due to improved signal-to-noise ratio. The identified charged exciton emitting at 1549.5 nm exhibits single-photon emission purity up to 94.7%, validated by a raw peak-area integration under pulsed quasi-resonant excitation. Under these conditions, photons emitted sequentially from the unprocessed planar structure reveal a raw two-photon interference visibility of 51% of the photon wave packet within the 2 ns time window and 41% over a 4 ns integration window, all without Purcell enhancement typical for cavity-embedded emitters. Combining broadband extraction, high photon coherence, and emitter preselection on a native III-V wafer, this architecture paves the way for marker-based deterministic fabrication of high-quality monolithic nanophotonic devices.

title: Piezo-Kerr effect in altermagnets and noncollinear antiferromagnets
abstract: Symmetry is usually viewed as a constraint on physical responses, but it can also be used to design the fields that control them. Here, we adopt the representation-matching principle used to identify conjugate fields of order parameters and apply it to response tensors. A linear coupling, the key ingredient for sign-switching control, is symmetry-allowed when a component (or a combination of components) of the control field and the selected response component share the same irreducible representation of the magnetic point group (MPG) of the system. Applied to the magneto-optical Kerr effect, this principle yields a piezo-Kerr effect, in which specific strain combinations activate a Kerr response forbidden in the unstrained state. Enumerating all 122 MPGs, we identify 16 groups in which the unstrained Kerr response is forbidden while a linear strain-induced contribution is allowed. These groups are realized by altermagnets and noncollinear antiferromagnets with symmetry-enforced vanishing net magnetization. The active strain channels and the associated first-order sign reversals follow directly from symmetry. First-principles calculations for bulk MnTe$_{2}$ and CoF$_{2}$, and Cr$_{2}$Se$_{2}$O and Cr$_{2}$Te$_{2}$O monolayers confirm these predictions. In these materials, the Kerr rotation vanishes without strain, whereas 0.5-3% strain produces rotations ranging from tens to hundreds of millidegrees, and reversing the matched strain channel reverses the Kerr sign. These results establish a general route to large and switchable Kerr responses emerging from symmetry-forbidden states in compensated magnets.

title: Chiroptical Valleytronic in SnSe
abstract: Quantum geometric properties of Bloch electrons play a central role in governing light-matter interactions and transport phenomena in solids. Here, we report quantum-geometric chiroptical selection rules that generate a helicity-dependent momentum-space population imbalance in the group-IV monochalcogenide SnSe. By combining time- and angle-resolved extreme-ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy with ab initio real-time simulations of photoexcited carrier dynamics, we identify valley-selective excitation at opposite crystal momenta arising from the breaking of time-reversal symmetry under circularly polarized illumination. We theoretically demonstrate that the magnitude of valley circular dichroism is strongly constrained by crystal symmetry through its influence on the quantum geometric tensor, the key quantity underlying valley optical selection rules. The resulting chiroptically induced valley polarization decays on sub-picosecond timescales through intervalley scattering mediated by electron-phonon coupling. Furthermore, we show theoretically that the population imbalance between valleys at opposite momenta gives rise to a helicity-reversible transient photocurrent. These findings provide microscopic insight into how quantum geometry governs valley-selective light-matter interactions, valley polarization, and photocurrent generation in van der Waals materials exhibiting hidden and transient symmetry breaking.

summaries.en: Time- and angle-resolved extreme-ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy combined with ab initio real-time simulations reveals helicity-dependent valley-selective excitation in SnSe arising from circularly polarized light breaking time-reversal symmetry, with the valley circular dichroism constrained by crystal symmetry through the quantum geometric tensor, decaying via electron-phonon intervalley scattering on sub-picosecond timescales, and theoretically producing a helicity-reversible transient photocurrent.

title: Intensity-driven Mott-like transition in a 2D Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite
abstract: Two-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper-type halide perovskites have emerged as promising cutting-edge nonlinear optical materials due to their strong excitonic effects and carrier-density-dependent optical responses. In this work, we investigate the nonlinear optical properties and ultrafast carrier dynamics of (BA)$_2$PbI$_4$ under infrared excitation, resonant with the two-photon energy of its excitonic transition. Using a nonlinear femtosecond Z-scan measurement with a 1030\,nm pump pulse, we observe a pronounced intensity-dependent evolution of the nonlinear absorption coefficient and the refractive index. With increasing pump intensity, a switch from saturable absorption to reverse saturable absorption emerges, suggesting an intensity-driven Mott-like transition. To elucidate the underlying carrier dynamics, intensity-dependent transient absorption spectroscopy was performed under the same excitation intensities. This reveals a long-lived charge carrier population above the estimated Mott density, reflecting a clear phase transition from an exciton-dominated regime to a dense electron-hole plasma regime. Moreover, such an intensity-driven, high, and switchable nonlinear optical response, along with a Mott-like transition under infrared pulse excitation, makes the 2D (BA)$_2$PbI$_4$ perovskites suitable for all-optical operation in the infrared regime.

summaries.en: Femtosecond Z-scan and transient absorption measurements on 2D (BA)2PbI4 under 1030 nm two-photon-resonant excitation reveal an intensity-driven Mott-like transition from exciton-dominated saturable absorption to a dense electron-hole plasma regime with reverse saturable absorption, enabling switchable all-optical operation in the infrared.

title: Donor-acceptor recombination in diamond
abstract: We re-examine several optical systems that have previously been attributed to donor-acceptor (D-A) recombination in diamond, including the broad 2.8 eV and 2.3 eV bands, and the sharp-lined series in the ranges 2.0-2.7 eV and 4.0-5.0 eV. In all cases, internal transitions at one or multiple defect centers provide a more consistent explanation of the experimental observations than the D-A model. The 2.3 eV case is marginal, where the key argument against the D-A recombination is the improbably low probability of tunneling between remote donors and acceptors in diamonds with very low concentrations of impurities (~0.1 ppm). A more realistic model for the 2.3 eV band and the associated phosphorescence and thermoluminescence phenomena is trapping of electrons and holes at nitrogen and boron defects, respectively, followed by recombination at a deep center, which is tentatively assigned to the nearest neighbor B-N pair.

title: Mn-deficient Ni-Mn-Ga alloys: phase transitions, magnetic properties, and disappearance of martensitic transformation
abstract: Composition gradients formed during directional solidification are generally considered undesirable in Ni-Mn-Ga magnetic shape-memory alloys. However, these gradients offer a highly effective platform for systematically investigating composition-property relationships under identical growth and heat-treatment conditions. To exploit this approach, one Mn-deficient and two near-stoichiometric Ni-Mn-Ga oligocrystals were grown by optical zone remelting and characterized by X-ray fluorescence mapping, optical microscopy, X-ray diffraction, low-field magnetic measurements, and vibrating-sample magnetometry. The ingots contained elongated grains and axial compositional gradients, primarily associated with the redistribution of Mn and Ga, whereas Ni remained relatively uniformly distributed. The martensitic and premartensitic transformation temperatures generally increased with increasing Mn content. Neither transformation was detected between 10 and 400 K in specimens containing 20.5-22.0 at.% Mn, all of which had $e/a < 7.40$. In contrast, both transformations were observed in the investigated specimens containing at least 22.1 at.% ($e/a \geq 7.46$). This abrupt change may indicate a possible electron-concentration threshold for the occurrence of these transformations. Saturation magnetization increased with Mn content up to 25.8 at.%, reaching 96.9 A m$^2$/kg at 10 K and 71.2 A m$^2$/kg at 300 K. Post-growth annealing increased the transition temperatures and changed the low-field magnetic response. The results indicate that composition-gradient oligocrystals serve as an effective platform for investigating the relationships between composition, structure, and magnetic properties in Ni-Mn-Ga alloys with the same processing history.

title: Robust PCA Study of TEM Images of Gold Nanospheres: Stable and Dynamic Closed Knot-Like Phase-Space Loops
abstract: In this study, we apply Robust PCA to transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of gold nanoparticles (GNPs) to decompose their geometrical, topological, and dynamical organization into static and dynamic knot-like phase-space loops. Dynamic loops show higher crossing numbers and longer rope lengths, while static loops show higher mean curvature. Although most Alexander determinants were D(t)=1 with isolated values of D(t)=3 at smaller nanoparticle diameters, implying that geometrical complexity does not require topological complexity. The different writhe signs indicate opposite handedness and distinct phase-space geometries in static and dynamic cases. For both static and dynamic knot-like loops, the graphs show an inverse relationship between mean curvature and mean torsion. Flatter trajectories occur at high curvature, and more torsional twisting occurs at low curvature. The small changes in Moffatt-Ricca helicities (~10^-14<<0) are due to circulation-dependent scaling, yet Moffatt-Ricca helicities still follow the same self-linking trend in both static and dynamic configurations. As nanoparticle diameter increases, the dynamic knot-like loops show stronger Kelvin-like spectral localization and smaller minimum self-approach distances, indicating more concentrated spatial modes and tighter geometric folding. At the same time, the decreasing CTEI suggests reduced global phase-space organization. These contrasting trends indicate that the geometrical organization tends to be less global and coherent, and more localized and mode-specific. These results show that the PCA-reconstructed phase space could serve as a mathematical analog to Kelvin's aether, because all disturbances exhibit similar topological configurations with varying degrees of geometric difference.

summaries.en: Robust PCA of TEM images of gold nanospheres decomposes their geometry and dynamics into static and dynamic closed knot-like phase-space loops that show opposite handedness and an inverse curvature–torsion relationship while retaining simple Alexander determinants, suggesting geometrical complexity without topological complexity.

title: Foundry-Fabricated Silicon Nitride Grating Arrays with Uniform Power Distribution at Visible Wavelengths
abstract: Multiplexed optical biosensors are widely deployed to read out many biological targets in parallel. However, their channel count and integration density are limited by the photonic network that delivers light to individual sensing sites. Existing on-chip networks have been largely developed for phased arrays and image projection, where performance is assessed through an aggregate radiation pattern rather than the local intensity at each output. In this Letter, we demonstrate a novel bus-and-tap network architecture for massively parallel multiplexed optical delivery. The network uses cascaded directional couplers with individually designed interaction lengths, allowing for arbitrary, user-defined illumination patterns not possible with conventional binary tree architectures. We experimentally validated our proposed architecture with 46 visible-wavelength grating emitter channels designed for uniform illumination at 40 $\mu$m pitch in a commercial 300-mm silicon nitride foundry process, achieving an emitted-intensity coefficient of variation of 9.3% at 530 nm, and 8.8% under band-integrated illumination from 550 nm to 650 nm. These results provide a route to scalable visible-light delivery for sensing, imaging, neural interfaces, and parallel optical addressing in quantum systems.

title: QuDPy-FDGF: A Python-Based Tool for Computing Ultrafast Nonlinear Optical Responses Using Frequency Domain Green's Functions
abstract: We present QuDPy-FDGF, an open-source Python framework that evaluates Liouville-space pathways as hybrid chains of time propagators and frequency-domain Green's functions. Frequency-resolved intervals are computed directly through shifted linear systems, without time propagation followed by a Fourier transform, while other intervals may remain in the time domain. A model-agnostic block interface separates the physical model from pathway construction, numerical propagation, and detection. The released implementation provides an explicit dense Liouville-space backend for reference calculations and a sector-resolved sparse backend using matrix-free generator actions, Krylov time propagation, and generalized minimal residual (GMRES) resolvent solves. Its observable layer reuses propagated pathway responses to evaluate operator expectation values, action-detected readout interactions, instantaneous jump rates, and integrated mean jump counts. The framework is assessed on an analytically solvable open two-level system and on two examples of increasing complexity: the complete third-order rephasing response, with its eight sequences, of a thermally initialized anisotropic Heisenberg (XXZ) spin chain with unequal excitation sectors, and two coupled dissipative anharmonic modes whose spectra depend on the detected observable, with the fifth-order double-quantum response of their closed limit. The calculations reproduce the analytical two-level response, check the matrix-free sparse evaluation against the dense assembly of the generator, and recover the harmonic-limit cancellation of the fifth-order signal when the required three-excitation manifold is retained. QuDPy-FDGF therefore provides a unified framework for pathway- and observable-resolved nonlinear spectroscopy in finite or truncated Hilbert spaces with unitary or Markovian Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) dynamics.

summaries.en: QuDPy-FDGF is an open-source Python framework that evaluates Liouville-space pathways as hybrid chains of time propagators and frequency-domain Green's functions computed via shifted linear systems, offering dense and sparse backends and an observable layer, and it is validated on an analytically solvable open two-level system, the third-order rephasing response of an anisotropic Heisenberg spin chain, and coupled dissipative anharmonic modes.

title: Laser with $7\times10^{-18}$ stability
abstract: We report a laser with record frequency stability, based on a 21 cm cryogenic silicon cavity. For best short-term stability, the cavity operates at 6 K to minimize Brownian thermal noise and achieves a fractional stability of $7\times10^{-18}$ between 2 to 50 s of averaging time and 2.5 mHz linewidth. For best long-term stability the cavity operates at 16 K, where silicon has a zero-crossing of thermal expansion. Slightly increased thermal noise limits the performance to $9\times10^{-18}$, consistent with the expected temperature scaling, but the long-term performance is improved. The laser then has a linewidth of 2.9 mHz and long-term frequency drift less than 4 {\mu}Hz s$^{-1}$. The laser is used to enhance the performance of a state-of-the-art Sr lattice clock, operating with Rabi and Ramsey interrogation times beyond 10 s.

title: Efficient third-harmonic generation in high-Q tantalum pentoxide microcavities
abstract: Nonlinear harmonic generation in microcavities offers a compelling route toward energy efficient on-chip short-wavelength coherent light sources, enabled by tight optical confinement within compact mode volumes and flexible dispersion engineering. Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) photonic platforms are particularly promising for realizing such nonlinear processes: their broad transparency window (280-8000 nm) supports broadband operation, their large bandgap suppresses two-photon absorption, and their thick-film deposition capability enables dispersion management--features that can collectively enhance the performance of nonlinear light sources. Here, we demonstrate, to the best of our knowledge, the first efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) in high-Q Ta2O5 microcavities. These microcavities feature smooth surfaces and high loaded Q factors up to 2.67X10^6, thereby facilitating nonlinear interactions. Through dispersion engineering, efficient THG is realized in both suspended microdisks and monolithic microrings under telecom-band continuous-wave laser pumping, as confirmed by optical spectra, visible-light microscopy, and the near-cubic pump-power dependence of the conversion efficiency. This work lays a foundation for chip-scale f-3f self-referencing of frequency combs and next-generation integrated nonlinear photonics.

title: Alignment-Free Optical Combining with Scalar-Message Expectation Propagation Detection for Distributed Multi-Aperture Coherent Reception
abstract: We propose an alignment-free distributed multi-aperture optical receiver with a single coherent front end, in which the differential delays between apertures are large. The branch signals are optically combined without inter-branch delay or phase alignment. Large differential delays produce separated tap clusters, forming a sparse ISI channel with long memory. Scalar-message expectation propagation exploits this sparsity to recover the transmitted symbols. Simulations show lower BER than equal-area single-aperture reception and no clear BER degradation over the tested delay spans. As the maximum differential delay increases from 100.5 to 200.5 symbol periods, the channel span nearly doubles, while the factor-graph edge count increases by only about 1.5\%. The trade-off is higher BER than ideal coherent combining schemes in exchange for fewer coherent front ends than digital combining and no inter-branch delay or phase alignment before optical combining.

summaries.en: The paper proposes an alignment-free distributed multi-aperture coherent optical receiver with a single coherent front end that optically combines branches with large differential delays without delay or phase alignment, using scalar-message expectation propagation to exploit the resulting sparse long-memory ISI channel, achieving lower BER than equal-area single-aperture reception and no clear BER degradation over tested delay spans while trading higher BER than ideal coherent combining for fewer coherent front ends than digital combining and no pre-combining alignment.

title: Metasurface engineering of transient photothermal responses for vibrational imaging at living interfaces
abstract: Chemical transformations at biological interfaces are central to cellular function, yet the weak vibrational signals associated with subtle molecular changes limit their spatially resolved observation. Here, we present metasurface-driven mid-infrared photothermal imaging (MetaMIP), which uses resonantly engineered metasurfaces to amplify molecular temperature modulation while retaining rapid thermal recovery. Visible-light detection converts this response into submicrometre maps of individual nanoparticles and biological cells. In living cells, MetaMIP resolves spatially distinct chemical changes during enzymatic lipid conversion across the cell membrane. These results demonstrate the potential of engineered photothermal interfaces for mapping chemical composition and tracking its evolution during reactions.

summaries.en: Metasurface-driven mid-infrared photothermal imaging (MetaMIP) amplifies molecular temperature modulation while retaining rapid thermal recovery, enabling submicrometre mapping of individual nanoparticles and living cells and resolving spatially distinct chemical changes during enzymatic lipid conversion at the cell membrane.

title: Reconfigurable Free-Space Optical Interconnects
abstract: Free-space optical interconnects can support many low-data-rate channels while avoiding the cost, energy consumption, and packaging constraints of optical waveguide- or fiber-based systems that are widely used today. We propose a free-space optical interconnect system based on reconfigurable micromirror arrays, and show that it scales favorably due to its two-dimensional scaling. We discuss the channel count scaling model, compare our demonstration with theory, and project a channel count above 10,000 to achieve 100 Tbps with slow channels (e.g., <10 Gbps). In a proof-of-concept system with a piston-motion micromirror array, we demonstrate nine channels that are simultaneously optimized. The optimization enables -21.7 dB of average worst-case crosstalk for a channel pitch equal to twice the beam radius, a smaller channel spacing than that required in flat tip-tilt mirrors. The optimization flow is further investigated for different channel spacings, simultaneous illumination, and different numbers of outputs, which generally achieve smaller worst-case crosstalk than the flat tip-tilt mirror case. Overall, the work demonstrates the advantage of piston-motion micromirrors in the proposed optical interconnects.

title: All-photonic millimeter-wave and terahertz signal core at room and cryogenic temperatures
abstract: Millimeter-wave and terahertz technologies offer new opportunities for high-capacity communications, sensing, and quantum systems, but electronic signal chains above 100 GHz are limited by weak sources, noisy receivers, and lossy interconnects. Photonic approaches mitigate these constraints by enabling chip-scale high-frequency components, yet existing implementations generally retain lossy off-chip electrical or free-space links, hindering dense and compact integration for cryogenic or space-constrained settings. Here, we show a monolithic lithium tantalate photonic chip, termed a signal core, which generates, modulates, routes, and detects continuous-wave signals at discrete frequencies between 100 GHz and 2.5 THz. The architecture integrates high-frequency functional modules on chip and uses exclusively fiber-based optical interfaces. Bidirectional coherent electro-optic conversion enables signal generation, detection, and nanosecond-scale amplitude and phase modulation, while micro-coplanar striplines interconnect the modules into an end-to-end signal chain on a single chip. Our modules achieve single-photon electro-optic coupling rates of g_0/2\pi=10 kHz and peak drive-power-normalized photon-flux conversion efficiencies of 1.0%/mW for generation and 0.5%/mW for detection. It also operates at 4 K in a dilution refrigerator through the same fiber-only optical links. Together, these capabilities establish an all-photonic platform for millimeter-wave-to-terahertz systems and offer a broadly applicable architecture for applications constrained by electrical-interconnect loss, heat load, and footprint.

title: Laser-design methodology for extending an available wavelength range of dual-wavelength injection-seeded laser
abstract: This paper describes a method for expanding the applicable wavelength range of dual-wavelength oscillation injection-locked lasers. Special focus is placed on the laser design that enables simultaneous oscillations at both the gain center and gain tail, requiring the most stringent requirements. We show that a sufficient performance can be achieved by introducing a wavelength-dependence property onto the output coupling mirror, without giving any losses in the laser resonator. We also show how we can determine such wavelength-dependent property on the basis of experimental measurements. Using the designed output-coupler, in practices, we demonstrate simultaneous oscillations with an equal output power, across a variety of wavelength combinations of near the gain center and around the gain tail in which the wavelength separation amounts 60 nm at the most.

summaries.en: A laser design methodology that adds wavelength-dependent properties to the output coupling mirror, without introducing resonator losses, enables dual-wavelength injection-seeded oscillation simultaneously at the gain center and gain tail with equal output power for wavelength separations up to 60 nm.

title: Intrinsic Angular Momentum Contribution to the Sagnac Response of a Rotating Helical Optical Fiber
abstract: We investigate rotation-induced phase accumulation of structured light in a mechanically rotating uniform helical optical fiber using a four-component optical Dirac-like equation. In the paraxial and weak-geometry regime, the intrinsic dynamics contain a torsion-induced geometric coupling and a mechanical rotation--angular-momentum coupling. We show that, in a common-path mirror-reflection geometry, both the torsion-induced geometric phase and the conventional area-dependent Sagnac contribution cancel over a complete round trip, whereas the intrinsic rotation--angular-momentum phase survives. The surviving phase depends on the intrinsic total angular momentum of the structured optical mode and provides a common-path interferometric route for probing intrinsic angular momentum effects in rotational sensing.

summaries.en: A four-component Dirac-like equation analysis shows that in a rotating uniform helical optical fiber, torsion-induced geometric and area-dependent Sagnac phases cancel over a complete common-path round trip, leaving an intrinsic rotation–angular-momentum phase that depends on the mode's total angular momentum and enables common-path interferometric rotational sensing.

title: Efficient Modeling of 3D-Printed Freeform Waveguides with a Transformation Optics-Based Beam Propagation Method
abstract: An efficient numerical method is introduced for simulating wave propagation in 3D-printed freeform waveguides, referred to as photonic wire bonds (PWBs). This approach integrates transformation optics (TO) with curvilinear meshing to map the original 3D freeform PWB structure onto a straight waveguide, which possesses anisotropic material characteristics. The resulting waveguide is then analyzed using an anisotropic full-vectorial beam propagation method (BPM). To validate the performance and effectiveness of the proposed TO-BPM algorithm, a comparison is made with the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique. Our approach reduces the simulation time by more than two orders of magnitude, depending on the degree of trajectory bending, in combination with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 3.9% in power transmission simulation relative to the FDTD.

title: The Mechanism of Chirality in Plasmonic Structures: Asymmetric Resonance Modes
abstract: This study presents a theoretical framework for understanding the mechanism of chirality generation and circular dichroism (CD) in chiral nanostructures, with a particular focus on the role of asymmetric plasmon resonance mode distributions. Although previous studies have linked chiroptical properties to resonance differences, the specific nature and origin of these differences have not been fully elucidated. Here, we provide a more detailed explanation by quantitatively analyzing the asymmetric electric-field components arising from mode asymmetry. Specifically, we examine the near-field symmetry of individual nanorods and corner-stacked coupled structures (CSCS). The results demonstrate that chirality arises from asymmetric electric-field distributions, which give rise to distinct phase and amplitude responses of the electromagnetic fields in the composite structure under right-handed circularly polarized (RCP) and left-handed circularly polarized (LCP) illumination. The absorption and CD spectra, which exhibit distinct features around $910\,\mathrm{nm}$, support this mechanism and provide valuable insights into the design of chiroptical materials. The proposed mechanism is not restricted to a specific chiral structure or resonance and offers a broader explanation for the generation of circular dichroism.

summaries.en: This study explains that chirality and circular dichroism in plasmonic nanostructures arise from asymmetric plasmon resonance mode distributions, which produce asymmetric electric-field components and distinct phase and amplitude responses under right- and left-handed circularly polarized illumination, as supported by absorption and CD spectra near 910 nm and demonstrated for individual nanorods and corner-stacked coupled structures.

summaries.ja: 本研究は、プラズモンナノ構造におけるキラリティーと円二色性が非対称なプラズモン共鳴モード分布に由来し、それが非対称な電場成分を生み出して右円偏光と左円偏光の照射下で異なる位相・振幅応答をもたらすことを明らかにし、910 nm付近の吸収・CDスペクトルおよび単一ナノロッドとコーナースタック結合構造によってこれを支持している。

title: Shaping Near Fields of Photonic Modes into Topological Textures
abstract: Topological textures of light, such as optical vortices and skyrmions, are attractive for high-density information encoding and light-matter interactions. In the near field, topologies have primarily been realized using polaritonic platforms that inherently tie the platform to the material dispersion, limiting their footprint due to propagation losses and restricting their operating spectral region. Here, we introduce a route to shape near-field topologies through the geometric engineering of a dielectric metasurface supporting a quasi-bound state in the continuum resonance, without the need for polaritonic surface waves. In-plane deformation of our metasurface bars conserves their resonance-driven near-fields locally, so that the metasurface geometry and the polarization of the illuminating light dictate the generated topology. By shaping silicon unit cells into geometries with rotational symmetry, we create optical topologies with controllable topological charge. Using phase-resolved scattering-type near-field optical microscopy, we experimentally characterize high-purity resonance-locked topologies such as vortices in concentric rings and topological charge doublets in Archimedean spirals. In contrast to conventional topological textures, our purely photonic mode-based field textures are stationary standing waves in the radial direction, without relying on surface-wave propagation or polaritonic dispersion, establishing a spectrally and spatially scalable platform for near-field topological photonics.

summaries.en: By geometrically engineering a dielectric metasurface that supports a quasi-bound state in the continuum resonance, the authors shape non-polaritonic near fields into controllable topological textures such as vortices and topological charge doublets, characterized with phase-resolved scattering-type near-field optical microscopy.

title: Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster study of systematic shifts and fine-structure constant sensitivity in {\rm Cf$^{17+}$}, {\rm Cm$^{15+}$} and {\rm Bk$^{16+}$} highly charged ions
abstract: Highly charged ions (HCIs) are among the most promising candidates proposed for the development of next-generation optical clocks and the precision tests of fundamental physics. In this work, we investigate the clock-relevant properties of $\rm Cf^{17+}$, $\rm Cm^{15+}$ and $\rm Bk^{16+}$ HCIs using Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster (FSRCC) theory. The corrections from Breit interaction, QED effects and perturbative triples are incorporated to improve the accuracy of results further. We compute excitation energies, transition amplitudes, lifetimes, hyperfine structure constants, electric quadrupole moments, and electric dipole polarizabilities for low-lying states of these ions. These properties are further used to characterize important clock transitions and estimate key systematic frequency shifts. Our calculations reveal that the proposed clock transitions exhibit strongly suppressed systematic frequency shifts. We also compute the sensitivity coefficients, $q$, and enhancement factors, $K_{\alpha}$, for the proposed clock transition as a probe to variation in the fine-structure constant, $\alpha$. Our calculations predict exceptionally large $K_{\alpha}$ of $-55.3$ and $57.5$ for $5f_{5/2} \rightarrow 6p_{1/2}$ transition in $\rm Cf^{17+}$ and $6p_{1/2} \rightarrow 5f_{5/2}$ transition in $\rm Bk^{16+}$, respectively. These giant $K_{\alpha}$s place the proposed transitions among the most sensitive optical probes for the laboratory searches for $\alpha$ variation. Further, a comparative analysis of proposed transitions in $\rm Cm^{15+}$ and $\rm Bk^{16+}$ shows that, $5f_{5/2} \rightarrow 5f_{7/2}$ transition possess smaller systematic shifts and is therefore attractive for precision frequency metrology, whereas $6p_{1/2} \rightarrow 5f_{5/2}$ transition exhibit significantly enhanced sensitivity to $\alpha$ variation.

summaries.en: Fock-space relativistic coupled-cluster calculations show that proposed clock transitions in Cf17+, Cm15+, and Bk16+ highly charged ions have strongly suppressed systematic frequency shifts, with exceptionally large fine-structure-constant sensitivity coefficients Kα of -55.
summaries.zh: 基于Fock空间相对论耦合簇计算，Cf17+、Cm15+和Bk16+高电荷态离子中提出的钟跃迁具有显著抑制的系统频移，并且Cf17+的5f5/2→6p1/2跃迁与Bk16+的6p1/2→5f5/2跃迁分别具有异常大的精细结构常数敏感系数Kα，为-55.
summaries.ja: Fock空間相対論的結合クラスター計算により、Cf17+、Cm15+、Bk16+の高電離イオンで提案された時計遷移は系統周波数シフトが強く抑制され、Cf17+の5f5/2→6p1/2遷移とBk16+の6p1/2→5f5/2遷移では微細構造定数感度係数Kαがそれぞれ-55.

title: AI Enhanced Cerenkov Luminescence Microscopy
abstract: Cerenkov Luminescence Microscopy (CLM) enables the visualization of radiotracer uptake in three-dimensional (3D) tumor spheroids but is limited by low photon statistics and spatial blurring caused by positron transport. Here, we present a Monte Carlo (MC)-guided deep learning framework for CLM image restoration. Using TOPAS/Geant4, we developed a physical model of heterogeneous 3D tumor spheroids to simulate positron transport, Cerenkov photon generation and optical propagation. A dataset of 15,360 paired degraded and idealized ground-truth (GT) images was generated from 80 simulated spheroid geometries and used to train a supervised Content-Aware Image Restoration (CARE) network. Compared with the self-supervised Noise2Void (N2V) denoising method, CARE achieved substantially lower reconstruction errors on synthetic validation data, reducing the mean squared error from 0.0492 to 0.0051. Training stability and noise robustness analyses further demonstrated high reproducibility of the restored images. The trained CARE model was subsequently applied to experimental CLM images acquired from 27 U87 tumor spheroids following 18F-FDG uptake. The restored images exhibited more localized intensity distributions and higher local contrast and signal-to-noise ratios compared with raw and N2V-processed images. These findings, aligned with the 3Rs principles of animal experimentation, demonstrate the potential of physics-based supervised restoration to mitigate both noise and positron-induced spatial broadening in CLM.

summaries.en: A Monte Carlo-guided supervised deep learning framework using a CARE network restores Cerenkov luminescence microscopy images of 3D tumor spheroids, reducing reconstruction error relative to Noise2Void and yielding more localized intensity distributions with higher local contrast and signal-to-noise ratios in experimental 18F-FDG U87 spheroid images.
summaries.zh: 一种基于蒙特卡罗引导的监督式深度学习框架采用CARE网络恢复三维肿瘤球体的切伦科夫发光显微图像，相比Noise2Void降低了重建误差，并在18F-FDG摄取的U87球体实验图像中获得更局域化的强度分布以及更高的局部对比度和信噪比。
summaries.ja: モンテカルロ法に導かれたCAREネットワークを用いた教師あり深層学習フレームワークは、三次元腫瘍スフェロイドのチェレンコフ発光顕微鏡画像を復元し、Noise2Voidと比較して再構成誤差を低減するとともに、18F-FDG取り込みU87スフェロイドの実験画像においてより局在化した強度分布と高い局所コントラストおよび信号対雑音比を実現した。

title: Second- and third-order nonlinearities in silicon nitride waveguides via heterogeneous integration of lithium niobate membranes
abstract: Thick, dispersion-engineered silicon nitride is a leading platform for integrated third-order nonlinear optics, supporting supercontinuum and frequency comb generation. However, it lacks the second-order nonlinearity required by many applications. Here we bond pre-fabricated x-cut thin-film lithium niobate membranes onto finished silicon nitride waveguides as a back-end step, compatible with commercially fabricated waveguides. A single silicon nitride waveguide generates an octave-spanning supercontinuum and, through the lithium niobate membrane, concurrent second-harmonic, sum- and difference-frequency generation. These results open new possibilities for thick silicon nitride photonics, from visible light generation to on-chip $f$-$2f$ comb self-referencing, a key step towards miniaturised timing and navigation quantum technologies.

summaries.en: By bonding pre-fabricated x-cut thin-film lithium niobate membranes onto finished silicon nitride waveguides as a back-end step, a single waveguide generates an octave-spanning supercontinuum while the membrane enables concurrent second-harmonic, sum- and difference-frequency generation, opening routes to visible light generation and on-chip f-2f comb self-referencing.
summaries.zh: 通过将预制好的x切薄膜铌酸锂膜作为后端工艺键合到已完成的氮化硅波导上，单个波导即可产生跨越一个倍频程的超连续谱，同时该铌酸锂膜实现同步的二次谐波、和频与差频产生，为可见光产生和片上f-2f梳自参考开辟了新途径。
summaries.ja: 予備作製したxカット薄膜ニオブ酸リチウム膜を後工程として完成済みの窒化ケイ素導波路上に貼り合わせることで、単一の導波路がオクターブにわたるスーパーコンティニュームを発生させるとともに、その膜を通じて第二高調波・和周波・差周波発生を同時に実現し、可視光生成やオンチップf-2fコム自己参照への道を開いた。

title: Extracting target-related flow structures using a time-lagged cross-correlation ranking criterion
abstract: Structures with large global contributions to a flow field are not necessarily those that are most closely associated with a specified engineering observable. We propose a time-lagged cross-correlation (TCC) ranking criterion to extract target-related dynamical structures from a fixed modal expansion while preserving existing spatial modes and temporal coefficients. The criterion ranks mode groups by the mean squared norm of cross-responses between their flow contributions and the observable over a lag window. It is tested separately using dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD). TCC-DMD analysis shows that TCC recovers three low-contribution target structures from a dominant background in a synthetic flow. The reconstruction error for the target subfield is 2.15\%. In the cylinder wake, different force observables select structures associated with the vortex-shedding fundamental, slow drag variations, and the second harmonic. In the cavity case, selected modes connect two main frequency bands of the target observable to distinct spatial amplitude and phase distributions. TCC-POD analysis shows that the criterion minimises the weighted truncation error of the correlation operator among equally sized subsets of the fixed orthogonal basis. A comparison with canonical correlation decomposition further reveals differences between fixed-direction selection and correlation-based basis construction in the spatial structure and retention of flow information. Lag aggregation can improve structure identification when zero-lag association is insufficient. The gains depend on the cross-response distribution and window selection. TCC separates target-related ranking from mode-set construction, enabling comparison of spatial structures associated with different observables within the same modal expansion.

summaries.en: The paper proposes a time-lagged cross-correlation ranking criterion that extracts target-related flow structures from a fixed modal expansion by ranking mode groups according to the mean squared norm of cross-responses with a specified observable over a lag window, demonstrated with DMD and POD.
summaries.zh: 该论文提出了一种时滞互相关排序准则，通过在滞后窗口内按模态组与指定可观测量的互响应均方范数进行排序，从固定模态展开中提取与目标相关的流动结构，并分别用DMD和POD进行了验证。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、遅れ窓内での指定された観測量との相互応答の平均二乗ノルムに基づいてモード群を順位付けすることで、固定されたモーダル展開から対象に関連する流れ構造を抽出する時間遅れ相互相関ランキング基準を提案し、DMDとPODでそれぞれ検証した。

title: A New Twist on Astigmatic Transformation: Beyond Laguerre-Gaussian Beams
abstract: Astigmatic transformation is widely used to convert the azimuthal phase structure of Laguerre-Gaussian vortex beams into intensity patterns from which the topological charge can be read out. Here, we show that this phase-to-intensity conversion is not just restricted to the Laguerre-Gaussian radial profile. We derive analytical expressions for the astigmatically transformed high-order Bessel--Gauss and perfect optical vortex fields, and find that, despite their substantially different radial structures, the number of intensity minima is directly set by the accumulated azimuthal phase winding. Numerical simulations and experimental measurements on both beam families confirm this result, establishing astigmatic transformation as a direct probe of the topological charge of scalar structured optical fields. We further extend the approach to non-separable vector Bessel-Gauss beams, in which the spatial and polarization degrees of freedom are coupled, and show that polarization-resolved detection allows the topological charge of the constituent spatial modes to be determined independently.

summaries.en: The paper shows analytically, numerically, and experimentally that astigmatic transformation converts the azimuthal phase winding of high-order Bessel-Gauss and perfect optical vortex beams into an intensity pattern whose number of minima directly gives the topological charge, and extends this phase-to-intensity probe to non-separable vector Bessel-Gauss beams via polarization-resolved detection.
summaries.zh: 该论文通过解析推导、数值模拟和实验证明，像散变换能将高阶贝塞尔-高斯光束和完美涡旋光束的方位相位缠绕转换为强度图样，其强度极小值数目直接给出拓扑电荷数，并将这一相位-强度探测方法借助偏振分辨探测推广至空间与偏振耦合的不可分离矢量贝塞尔-高斯光束。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、非点収差変換が高次ベッセル・ガウスビームおよび完全光渦ビームの方位方向の位相巻き数を、極小点の数がトポロジカルチャージを直接与える強度パターンへ変換することを解析・数値・実験で示し、さらに偏光分解検出により空間自由度と偏光自由度が結合した非分離ベクトルベッセル・ガウスビームへこの位相-強度プローブを拡張した。

title: Predictive electronic feedback control for narrow-linewidth lasers
abstract: Narrow-linewidth lasers are essential for various key atom-laser interaction processes and optical setups in quantum coherent control, quantum precision measurement, and quantum information science. The Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique is the standard method for the frequency-stabilization of narrow-linewidth lasers, but the inherent time delay in its feedback loop inevitably induces excessive phase noise, commonly known as servo bumps. Previous solutions primarily rely on additional optical components outside the electronic feedback control loop. Here, we propose and implement a generic method based on the Smith predictor to address the time-delay issue entirely within the electronic part of the PDH feedback control loop. We systematically demonstrate its capability to suppress phase noise and reduce servo bumps by adding only a single Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) controller to the loop. This class of methods is demonstrated to be conceptually concise with minimal hardware overhead, effective in practice, and holds potential for a wide variety of future applications.

summaries.en: The authors propose and implement a Smith-predictor-based predictive electronic feedback control method that mitigates the time-delay-induced phase noise and servo bumps in Pound-Drever-Hall frequency stabilization of narrow-linewidth lasers using only a single added FPGA controller.
summaries.zh: 作者提出并实现了一种基于史密斯预估器的预测性电子反馈控制方法，仅通过增加一个FPGA控制器，就在Pound-Drever-Hall反馈环路内抑制了窄线宽激光器稳频中由时间延迟引起的相位噪声和伺服凸起。
summaries.ja: 著者らは、スミス予測器に基づく予測型電子フィードバック制御法を提案・実装し、FPGAコントローラを1台追加するだけで、窄線幅レーザーのPound-Drever-Hall周波数安定化における時間遅延由来の位相雑音とサーボバンプを抑制できることを示した。

title: Analytical Modeling of Modulated Heating for Three-Dimensional Anisotropic Optical Thermometry of Multilayered Cylinders
abstract: Thermally relevant cylindrical geometries are used in a plethora of applications with thermal property differences depending significantly on material complexity. Manu- facturing processes also induce substantial anisotropy ratios resulting in directionally dependent thermal transport. However, for cylindrical specimens, current thermal metrology resolves only isotropic thermal properties, assumes perfect thermal inter- faces, and offers no formulation for temperature spatial dependence. In this work, we present an analytical framework that models the frequency dependent thermal transport of orthotropic arbitrary layered cylinders to be used as a forward model for existing optical thermometry techniques. This formulation captures the effects of non-negligible thermal boundary conductance and offers the first closed-form solution of a projected Gaussian laser, a common form of heating in thermal metrology, hav- ing a finite elliptic spot size on a curved surface. The novel anisotropic cylindrical model was compared with literature derivations involving two-dimensional isotropic transport for cylinders by applying simplifying assumptions. For single- and two- layerisotropicsamples, thethree-dimensionalmodelagreedwithestablishedsolutions with negligible error, while predictions for orthotropic multilayer samples agreed with finite-element simulations within 1.5% across a range of material properties and laser geometries. Comparison with anisotropic planar models identified conditions under which a planar approximation can reduce computation time. These results estab- lish the first forward model for noncontact characterization of anisotropic thermal properties in arbitrarily layered cylinders.

summaries.en: This work presents an analytical framework that models frequency-dependent thermal transport in orthotropic arbitrarily layered cylinders, incorporating finite thermal boundary conductance and the first closed-form solution for a projected Gaussian laser with a finite elliptic spot on a curved surface, for use as a forward model in optical thermometry.
summaries.zh: 本研究提出了一个解析框架，用于模拟正交各向异性任意分层圆柱体的频率相关热输运，其中纳入了不可忽略的热边界导纳，并首次给出了曲面上一有限椭圆光斑投影高斯激光的闭式解，可作为光学测温的正向模型。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、無視できない熱境界コンダクタンスを考慮し、曲面上の有限楕円スポットを持つ投影ガウスレーザーの初の閉形式解を提供する、直交異方性の任意積層円柱における周波数依存熱輸送をモデル化する解析的枠組みを提示し、光学サーモメトリーの順モデルとして用いるものである。

title: Nanopillar metasurfaces uniting high optical reflectivity with ultracoherent nanomechanics
abstract: Mechanically compliant mirrors are key components in cavity optomechanics. However, the requirements to achieve the best optical and mechanical performance are usually in direct competition. A high reflectivity for tightly focused beams entails thick reflectors, whereas ultracoherent flexural nanomechanics necessitates thin membranes. We eliminate this trade-off by introducing high-refractive-index nanopillar metasurfaces on top of a thin membrane. We pattern a 50 micrometer-diameter array of nanopillars to form a photonic crystal. The flat band behavior of guided resonances in the photonic crystal enables a reflectivity of 99.82(1)% for a tightly focused beam of 7 micrometer waist. The combination of two guided resonances creates a 100 nanometer-wide high-reflectivity band around 1550 nanometer. Simultaneously, the nanopillar patterning realizes a density-modulated phononic crystal that isolates an ultracoherent localized mechanical mode with a $Q\cdot f$-product of $2\cdot 10^{14}$Hz. The demonstrated nanopillar metasurfaces enable lightweight mirrors for room-temperature quantum optomechanics and for use as levitated mirrors or lightsails.

summaries.en: High-refractive-index nanopillar metasurfaces patterned on a thin membrane form photonic and phononic crystals that simultaneously achieve 99.
summaries.zh: 在薄膜上图案化高折射率纳米柱超表面形成光子晶体和声子晶体，可同时对紧聚焦的7微米光束实现99.
summaries.ja: 薄膜上に高屈折率ナノピラー・メタサーフェスをパターニングしてフォトニック結晶とフォノニック結晶を形成することで、7マイクロメートルの集光ビームに対して99.

title: Observation of Polarization Topology in Magneto-Optical BICs
abstract: Polarization topology in momentum space is a fundamental characteristic of photonic bound states in the continuum (BICs), where the winding of far-field polarization defines a quantized topological charge. Although magneto-optical (MO) BICs combine polarization topology with magnetically tunable chirality, experimental characterization remains challenging because time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking complicates eigenpolarization extraction. Here, we experimentally resolve the momentum-space polarization topology of an MO BIC by reconstructing its two-dimensional far-field eigenpolarization texture. We extract the resonant output polarization using singular value decomposition of the polarization-resolved angle-resolved reflection matrix without invoking reciprocity. The reconstructed polarization azimuth winds counterclockwise by 2$\pi$ around the $\Gamma$-point singularity, yielding a topological charge of q = +1. Moreover, the polarization handedness can be reversed solely by varying the magnetic-bias strength, while the field direction and the measured topological charge remain unchanged. A non-Hermitian coupled-mode model traces this reversal to hybridization between the BIC mode and a leaky mode. This work establishes experimental access to momentum-space polarization topology in nonreciprocal photonics, opening a route to explore topological singularities and their evolution under active TRS breaking.

summaries.en: By reconstructing the two-dimensional far-field eigenpolarization texture of a magneto-optical bound state in the continuum using singular value decomposition of the polarization-resolved angle-resolved reflection matrix, the authors observe a counterclockwise 2π winding of the polarization azimuth around the Γ-point singularity with topological charge q = +1, and show that the polarization handedness can be reversed solely by varying the magnetic-bias strength while the topological charge remains unchanged.
summaries.zh: 通过利用偏振分辨角分辨反射矩阵的奇异值分解重建磁光连续域束缚态（BIC）的二维远场本征偏振织构，作者观测到偏振方位角围绕Γ点奇点逆时针缠绕2π、拓扑荷为q = +1，并证明仅通过改变磁偏置强度即可反转偏振手性而拓扑荷保持不变。
summaries.ja: 偏光分解角度分解反射行列の特異値分解を用いて磁気光学連続体中束縛状態（BIC）の二次元遠方場固有偏光テクスチャを再構成することで、著者らはΓ点特異点の周りに偏光方位角が反時計回りに2π巻き付き、トポロジカルチャージがq = +1となることを観測し、磁気バイアス強度を変えるだけで偏光のヘリシティを反転でき、トポロジカルチャージは不変であることを示した。

title: GEM-PIC-RZ: a Galilean electromagnetic particle-in-cell code in quasi-cylindrical geometry with nonuniform grids
abstract: Laser-plasma accelerators span scales from the micrometre wavelength of the driving laser to acceleration lengths of millimetres or metres. Full particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations resolve the laser carrier but are constrained by the Courant condition, whereas quasi-static models are computationally efficient but do not resolve it. We present GEM-PIC-RZ, a quasi-cylindrical implementation of the Galilean electromagnetic PIC scheme. The method retains the slow evolution of the forward field and therefore resolves the laser carrier while allowing a propagation step governed by the evolution of the laser and plasma rather than by the cell size. User-defined nonuniform grids and a charge-conserving regularization of the bubble closure support efficient simulations across these scales. Comparisons with the full PIC code FBPIC show agreement for the laser wake, the depletion and redshift of a few-cycle pulse, and ionization injection; the measured CPU time is about 2\,\% of that for FBPIC in the reported runs; the injected charge carries a model uncertainty of about 15\,\% from the regularization. An envelope model, in contrast, underestimates the depletion of the few-cycle pulse fivefold. Self-injection in a sharp density down-ramp is not yet reproduced and remains an open problem.

summaries.en: GEM-PIC-RZ is a quasi-cylindrical Galilean electromagnetic particle-in-cell code that resolves the laser carrier, permits propagation steps governed by laser and plasma evolution rather than cell size, supports user-defined nonuniform grids and charge-conserving regularization, agrees with FBPIC on laser wake, few-cycle pulse depletion and redshift, and ionization injection while running in about 2% of FBPIC's CPU time, though self-injection in sharp density down-ramps remains unreproduced.
summaries.zh: GEM-PIC-RZ 是一种准柱几何的伽利略电磁粒子模拟代码，能够分辨激光载波，其传播步长由激光与等离子体演化而非网格尺寸决定，支持用户自定义非均匀网格和电荷守恒正则化，在激光尾波、少周期脉冲耗尽与红移以及电离注入方面与 FBPIC 结果一致，运行 CPU 时间约为 FBPIC 的 2%，但尚不能重现陡峭密度下降沿中的自注入。
summaries.ja: GEM-PIC-RZは準円筒座標系のガリレイ電磁粒子シミュレーションコードであり、レーザー搬送波を分解しつつセルサイズではなくレーザーとプラズマの時間発展に支配される伝播ステップを可能にし、ユーザー定義の非一様格子と電荷保存正則化を備え、レーザー航跡、数サイクルパルスの depletion と赤方偏移、電離注入についてFBPICと一致し、CPU時間は約2%であるものの、急峻な密度下降ランプでの自己注入は未再現の課題として残る。

title: Confinement of hybridized light modes in nonlinear-optical superpotentials
abstract: In this work, we present a spatial and temporal light trapping mechanism induced by coherent frequency conversion. We consider a wave-mixing process, where a pumped nonlinearity mediates a frequency-domain beamsplitter interaction between two signal modes. When these wave modes are counterpropagating, temporally trapped eigenmodes emerge at the zero of the nonlinearity profile. We establish that such spatio-temporal trapping has a direct connection to supersymmetric quantum mechanics, which ensures the existence and robustness of the trapped modes and allows us to derive analytic solutions of the bound eigenmodes. Backwards sum-frequency conversion may thus enable a unique class of active photonic memory devices, whose design parameters are compatible with the state of the art in integrated nonlinear photonics. We propose proof-of-principle experiments to study this nonlinear-optical trapping effect on thin-film lithium niobate. In addition, as a case study, we show how the temporal trap can be used alongside parametric gain. Our work unveils potential applications ranging from classical integrated photonics to multimode quantum nonlinear photonics.

summaries.en: A coherent frequency-conversion wave-mixing process with counterpropagating signal modes is shown to temporally trap light at the zero of the nonlinearity profile, with supersymmetric quantum mechanics guaranteeing robust trapped eigenmodes and enabling analytic solutions, proposed for thin-film lithium niobate integrated photonics and compatible with active photonic memory.
summaries.zh: 研究表明，在信号模式反向传播的相干频率转换混波过程中，光会在非线性分布零点处被时间局域化，超对称量子力学保证了俘获本征模的存在性与鲁棒性并可解析求解，该机制可在薄膜铌酸锂上验证并有望用于有源光子存储器。
summaries.ja: 信号モードが逆伝搬するコヒーレントな周波数変換波混合過程において、非線形性プロファイルの零点で光が時間的に捕捉され、超対称量子力学が捕捉固有モードの存在と頑健性を保証して解析解を与え、薄膜ニオブ酸リチウム上での実証や能動フォトニックメモリへの応用が期待される。

title: Photon localization: Local measurements, localized states, and causality
abstract: We review what it means for a relativistic particle to be localized and argue that the most useful approach is through local measurement. This perspective ties localization directly to relativistic causality and measurable outcomes in spacetime. Strict localization in quantum field theory is formalized by states that give the same expectation value as vacuum for all local observables outside some spacetime region. With this formalism, single photons cannot be strictly localized, but coherent states can. The structure and interpretation of local observables and local operator algebras are discussed in connection with the Reeh-Schlieder theorem. Since probabilities of local measurement outcomes cannot vanish in vacuum, particle detection events must be phrased carefully. Key characteristics of strictly localized states are surveyed alongside concrete strategies for constructing them. The relationship between localization, causality, and on-demand sources is analyzed, finding that strictly localized states can represent localized, propagating information in quantum field theory. Explicit examples of localized photonic states are presented with an emphasis on quantum optics, including states that approximate single photons and (entangled) Bell states.

summaries.en: This review argues that the most useful notion of photon localization in relativistic quantum field theory is defined through local measurement and relativistic causality, showing that while single photons cannot be strictly localized, coherent states and certain localized photonic states—including approximations to single photons and entangled Bell states—can be, with strictly localized states capable of representing localized propagating information.
summaries.zh: 该综述提出，相对论量子场论中光子局域化最有用的概念应通过局域测量与相对论因果性来定义，并表明单光子无法被严格局域化，而相干态以及某些局域光子态（包括单光子近似态和纠缠贝尔态）可以实现严格局域化，且严格局域态能够表示局域传播的信息。
summaries.ja: 本レビューは、相対論的量子場理論における光子の局在化の最も有用な定式化は局所測定と相対論的因果性を通じて与えられ、単一光子は厳密には局在化できないがコヒーレント状態や一部の局在光子状態（単一光子の近似状態やもつれベル状態を含む）は厳密に局在化可能であり、厳密に局在化した状態は局在して伝播する情報を表し得ると論じている。

title: Time-reversal-based quantum metrology in a central-spin architecture: from SATIN to butterfly echo
abstract: We investigate quantum-enhanced time-reversal-based metrology using the central spin model, in which a single ancilla spin of magnitude $S_{\rm cen}$ mediates interactions between $N$ bath spins through a star-graph topology. We demonstrate that the SATIN (Signal Amplification Through Time-reversal Interaction) echo protocol can be implemented in this setup to achieve a Fisher information of $N^2/e$ with the collective $\langle J_y\rangle$ readout, corresponding to a $4.34\,\mathrm{dB}$ offset from the Heisenberg limit. Furthermore, we establish that this platform provides a pathway to perform the butterfly echo protocol by conjugating each evolution step with a random collective bath rotation, thereby achieving axis-agnostic Heisenberg-scaled sensing. Crucially, with a small $N-$independent number of random steps, the butterfly echo reaches a Fisher information of $N^2/4$ ($6\,\mathrm{dB}$ below the Heisenberg limit) for any unknown encoding axis, with the plateau gain tracking the Haar limit. Finally, we demonstrate that the central-spin magnitude $S_{\rm cen}$ provides a powerful knob to reduce the optimal protocol timescale without altering the metrological ceiling or the circuit depth required to reach isotropy. The proposed scheme is relevant to cavity QED and NMR quantum processors, where the central spin architecture arises naturally.

title: Entanglement certification of attosecond light fields with photoelectron interferometry
abstract: The emergence of entangled quantum optical states in high-harmonic generation raises a fundamental problem about its characterization, namely, \textit{how can entanglement of extreme-ultraviolet radiation be certified for attosecond light fields?} Here, we provide experimentally accessible separability tests, particularly showing that attosecond photoelectron interferometry provides a direct solution to this problem. This is achieved by a quantum optical treatment of mapping photoelectron interferometry to the measurement of optical correlation functions. This yields a negative-partial-transpose witness for infrared-XUV entanglement and a sufficient witness of genuine multipartite entanglement without auxiliary optical measurements. We evaluate both witnesses on explicit optical states and identify how the protocol can be extended to XUV-XUV entanglement certification. Hence, we establish attosecond photoelectron interferometry as a general framework for entanglement certification across a wide range of optical frequencies.

summaries.en: This paper shows that attosecond photoelectron interferometry provides experimentally accessible separability tests, including a negative-partial-transpose witness for infrared-XUV entanglement and a sufficient witness of genuine multipartite entanglement without auxiliary optical measurements, establishing a general framework for entanglement certification across optical frequencies.

title: High-fidelity entanglement of two spectrally-distinct solid state emitters
abstract: Solid state quantum emitters with electronic spin properties can be entangled using optical interferometric which-path erasure techniques that rely on identical frequencies and linewidths of the emitters. This promises a powerful, fast and scalable platform for quantum technologies. Using current protocols, a pair of emitters embedded in a waveguide interferometer can be deterministically prepared in a maximally entangled state. However, the amount of entanglement diminishes rapidly with increasing separation of the emission lines and variations in the linewidths of the emitters. Solid state emitters such as quantum dots are subject to intrinsic variations in the fabrication process. Therefore, manufacturing the required number of identical emitters on a chip is not scalable. In this Letter, we present a method that uses readily available pairs of entangled photons to entangle solid state emitters with large transition frequency separations and linewidth variations, circumventing the need to fabricate optically identical emitters. We demonstrate a concurrence of C = 0.95 for typical quantum dots using narrowband photon inputs.

title: SciFusion: Physics-Guided Compositional Diffusion for Multimodal 3D Scientific Image Generation
abstract: Existing 3D generative approaches are typically developed for individual imaging modalities, requiring substantial modality-specific data and limiting their ability to exploit shared structure across scientific imaging domains. We present SciFusion, a multimodal framework for unified 3D scientific image generation built on a latent diffusion backbone, with two key contributions. First, we introduce a compositional conditioning scheme that factorizes each modality into domain, object, and contrast representations. Sharing these factors across related modalities enables knowledge transfer across heterogeneous imaging domains and allows the factors to be recombined at inference time to synthesize unseen domain-object-contrast compositions in a zero-shot manner. Second, we incorporate domain-specific physics-informed objectives: Fourier spectral consistency for MRI, Radon projection consistency for CT, and multislice diffraction consistency for electron microscopy, to encourage generated samples to respect modality-dependent image formation processes. Extensive experiments across 15 medical and scientific imaging modalities demonstrate that SciFusion improves generation fidelity and cross-domain generalization over modality-specific and flattened multimodal conditioning strategies, while enabling zero-shot synthesis of unseen compositions without training on those target compositions. These results demonstrate that compositional, physics-guided conditioning provides a scalable framework for unified 3D scientific image generation, particularly for emerging modalities where large-scale training data are difficult to obtain.
subjects: Image and Video Processing (eess.IV) ; Machine Learning (cs.LG)

title: Electromagnetic Modeling of Deformation-Based Pinching Antennas
abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PAS) rely on local perturbations of a guiding structure to radiate part of the guided electromagnetic energy, making the physical response of the resulting pinching antenna (PA) fundamental to both guided-wave propagation and free-space radiation. To capture this coupled behavior, we develop an electromagnetic model of a finite deformation-based PA that directly relates the applied waveguide perturbation to its complex reflection and transmission responses and three-dimensional radiation characteristics. Full-wave MEEP simulations validate the model and demonstrate how the pinching ratio and pinched-section length jointly affect the transmitted power and phase, radiation power-fraction, and radiation pattern, thereby establishing PA geometry as a degree of freedom for controlling the radiation response. Importantly, this geometric dependence extends to communication performance, as the received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) results reveal that neither minimizing the PA--user distance nor maximizing the radiation power-fraction necessarily yields the highest SNR, since the applied perturbation also determines the realized gain toward the user.

summaries.en: An electromagnetic model of deformation-based pinching antennas is developed that directly links the applied waveguide perturbation to complex reflection and transmission responses plus three-dimensional radiation, validated by full-wave MEEP simulations showing how pinching ratio and pinched-section length jointly control transmitted power and phase, radiation power-fraction, and radiation pattern, with received-SNR results demonstrating that neither minimizing PA-user distance nor maximizing radiation power-fraction necessarily yields the highest SNR because the perturbation also sets the realized gain toward the user.
